summary: Florida Venetia tower near Venice, built 1956 per a 1969 paper, staffed to 1988, dismantled March 2019 and moved to Upper Esopus, NY; no source describes the Venice site now.

facts.design: Steel observation tower with 106 steps (1969 and 1988 newspapers); a 2019 project page calls it an MC-39 model
facts.status_note: Dismantled in March 2019 and taken to the Catskills Visitor Center in Mount Tremper, NY, where it opened as the Upper Esopus Fire Tower.

Constructed in 1956 per the 1969 Tampa Tribune; a 2019 project page estimates the mid-1940s instead
District forester said the tower would lose its full-time spotter in November 1974
Division spokesman said the tower would not close; federal civil-service jobs money restored full staffing
A state forest ranger was still climbing the tower to watch for fires, per a 1988 Tampa Tribune article
Dismantled for removal in March 2019; parts shipped to New York
Bought by Davana LLC for $1,000; opened in October 2019 as the Upper Esopus Fire Tower at the Maurice D. Hinchey Catskills Visitor Center

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1969 Tampa Tribune, as transcribed by Forest Lookouts, says 1956. The 2019 project page estimates the mid-1940s with no record cited. The story uses 1956.

The 2019 project page says the tower was decommissioned in the 1970s. The 1974 and 1975 reports describe full-time staffing and a 1988 article describes a ranger still climbing it. The story follows the newspapers.
The 1969 and 1988 newspapers give 85 feet; the 2019 project page gives 80 feet as the model's height. The story and height_m use 85 feet.
A 1969 article places the tower on US 41 between Venice and Englewood; a 1974 report places it on State Road 775 about four miles south of Venice. Both are reported.

notes_for_editor: No source describes what remains at the Venice site today or whether it is public; the company page says housing now surrounds the site. The galvanizing company page is a single account, and its Davana details are not confirmed elsewhere in these reads. The New York record us-ny-venetia-at-upper-esopus gives height_m 24.0 from OpenStreetMap, which conflicts with the 85-foot newspaper figure; that record should be checked. Florida access is not stated, so it is left out.
